sections.title: Judgment on Moab, Judah, and Israel

blocks.text: Amos 2 announces judgment on Moab, Judah, and Israel. The repeated phrase 'for three transgressions, and for four' presents accumulated offense rather than a literal count. The accusations move from Moab's violence to Judah's rejection of the LORD's law and then to Israel's sale of the righteous and needy, exploitation of the poor, sexual wrongdoing, abuse of pledged garments, and profanation of worship. The chapter closes by recalling the LORD's past acts and announcing that no human strength will escape judgment.

sections.title: Why Israel's social treatment is central

blocks.text: Amos's accusations against Israel are not general criticism of poverty or wealth. They name practices in which powerful people sell the righteous and needy, trample poor people, and misuse pledged clothing and religious settings. The chapter's ethical focus is exploitative practice and the distortion of justice; it does not authorize collective ethnic blame or private vengeance in the prophet's name.
